the role of caldesmon in the stabilization of actin filamnets in vivo and the possible role of caldesmom in cell motility and tumor metastasis.
the role of caldesmon in actin-based cellular motility and the mechanism by which it may modulate actin cytoskeletal dynamics.
the role of CaD39 and CaD40 fragments in modulating the actin cytoarchitecture of CHO cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CaD39 expression in CHO cells stabilizes microfilaments by enhancing TM's binding to actin in vivo.
caldesmon fragments containing the actin-binding domain, CaD40, and the Ca2+/CaM-binding domain, CaM39, can modulate the actin cytoplasmic microfilament system.
the CaD39 fragment is able to bind to actin filaments and tropomyosins in vitro and in vivo, thus enhancing TM-actin interactions and stabilizing microfilament bundles in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
caldesmon is an important regulator of actin filament dynamics and that it is a component of the actin-based motile machinery.
caldesmon is an actin-binding protein with multiple binding domains, which can modulate actin-based motile processes.
CaD39 is able to stabilize endogenous tropomysoin and microfilament structures in transfected CHO cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CaD39, a fragment containing only the actin-binding, Ca++/calm, and TM-binding domains of fibroblast caldsemon, is able to modulate actin cytoskeletal organization in vivo.
caldesmon fragments can modulate actin-based motile events and can affect the turnover rate of TM in vivo.
